reason: The revision adopts the required partial correction. It preserves the exact single original delegation and express activation, records the formal revocation as a later event, and withholds the sole earliest end, whole-order end, savings and final search closure pending the concrete section 411 statutory-history and 1980 transition investigation. It does not infer an earlier date or treat independent salary, leave or particular-office provisions as proof of unchanged classification power. The frozen original rejection remains valid and preserved.
accepted_findings: One original command delegates the President’s section 411 four-class chief-of-mission position classification power to the Secretary of State. The exact original operative paragraph and effective sentence remain intact; adjacent EOs 9800/9801 are excluded.
Express activation is November 13, 1946, rather than the November 8 signature. The complete order has no own-term sunset, deadline, reporting trigger or one-time completion condition.

The complete EO12292 section 10(b) formally revokes EO9799; section 11 makes that action effective as of February 15, 1981. The signature on February 23 and publication on February 25 are not substituted. This supports termination by that date and the no status, not the first cessation of the sole statutory power.

EO12292 preamble and section 2(c) identify a concrete statutory transition from 1946 Act section 411 to 1980 Act section 401 in related leave authority. The quoted substitution is not itself proof of when the classification delegation first ceased or whether statutory savings continued particular effects.

The related leave, compensation, particular-office and new statutory delegation analyses are unchanged in the bounded workpaper and remain qualified. The original named and numeric search scopes are exactly retained there, including the USC coverage boundary; no adequate-search or complete savings conclusion is carried into the revised claim.

quoted_parts:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, including the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (94 Stat. 
2071; 22 U.S.C. 3901 et seq .), and in order to conform existing Executive Orders 
to changes resulting from that Act, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Sec. 2. Section 1 of Executive Order No. 10471 is amended as follows:
(a) strike out “section 202(c) of the Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951, as 
added by the act of July 2, 1953, Public Law 102, 83rd Congress” and insert in 
lieu thereof “section 6305(b) of title 5 of the United States Code”;
(b) strike out “said section 202(c)(2)” and insert in lieu thereof “said section 
6305(b)”;
(c) strike out “section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946” and insert in lieu 
thereof “section 401 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3961)”.
